thread:
eli: Noticing a spike in attach latency + errors in eu-west3, looks correlated with a deep-scrub compaction run across AZs. GPU jobs stuck in Pending.
ops-bot: alert: attach-errors eu-west3 (sev: high) 50 failures in 10m; node-nvme queue-depth 120 average.
sam: can someone paste nvme stats?
maria: quick sample from affected node:
```
$ iostat -x 1 3
Device            r/s     w/s   rkB/s   wkB/s  avgqu-sz await  svctm  %util
nvme0n1         120.0  10500  2400   320000   18.7    22.4   1.05   96.3
nvme1n1          80.0   8200  1600   256000   14.2    19.1   0.98   88.7
```
priya: compaction job launched with global-window=0..90 concurrency=8 across AZs, which is bad because windows overlap and push cluster-wide IOPS.
tony: short fixes: 1) kube cordon a small set of janitor pods (not nodes) to break synchronization, 2) apply `--io-rate=4000` and `--max-concurrency=1` to janitor and rollout canary 5% nodes, 3) add temporary prewarm pool for GPU attaches.
eli: agree. can we instead stagger compaction by AZ quickly? that way we don't stop cleaning entirely.
priya: stagger plan: shift window offset by 30s per AZ using env var `SCRUB_AZ_OFFSET`. I can push change.
sam: for immediate recovery, do the canary change first. tony create dedicated pool?
tony: created `dedicated-buffer-eu-west3-1` (3 GPUs) and flipped routing for new attach requests.
ops-bot: metric: gpu-attach-failures 50 -> 6 (6m after routing + canary). scratch-scrub-backlog +190.
maria: i've rolled canary to 20% and watching latency. attach queue dropping.
eli: note we should not scale janitor replicas to 0; we want controlled housekeeping. backlog tracked in ticket INF-7682.
priya: rolling AZ-offset change now, will verify no overlapping windows.
sam: long-term note: either upgrade NVMe to higher IOPS SKUs in eu-west3 or isolate scrub to lower priority scheduling class. both require planning.
tony: logging follow-up: add a new metric `janitor.concurrent_writes` and alert if per-node avgque > 30.
eli: ok keeping thread open for 2h. if backlog >1000 open postmortem. :eyes:
